label: Justifying machine spend
title: From token maximising to cost consciousness
thesis: Machine work is becoming a managed operating expense that engineering organisations plan, attribute and defend — the way they already do headcount. As consumption outruns falling unit prices, the questions shift from which model is best to what a resolved task costs, who is accountable for the spend, and which work is worth running a machine on at all.
currentPressure: Per-developer token consumption has risen far faster than unit prices have fallen, so cheaper inference has produced larger bills rather than smaller ones.

implications.statement: Engineering budgets acquire a variable, consumption-driven line item that behaves unlike either headcount or conventional infrastructure.
Leaders become accountable for cost per resolved task, not just for delivery speed, and need attribution they mostly do not yet have.
Deciding whether a task is worth machine effort becomes a routine judgement developers make many times a day.

evidence.note: ~18x per-developer usage in nine months against a ~60% unit price fall
a standards body forming around AI infrastructure economics, backed by ten large enterprises
two independent cost analyses converge on cost per resolved task as the right unit of account
more reasoning tokens rarely buy better code but always cost more
open-weight models at roughly a third of the inference cost change the price floor
near-universal weekly use with cost concerns rising among practitioners

Cost of long-horizon agent loops grows quadratically with session length under naive context re-injection; exact-prefix caching cuts input cost by up to ~90% (41–80% in practitioner reports). Two teams on the same model can differ ~10x on cost from loop design alone.

Production telemetry: system prompts consume 69% of input tokens but only 28% of LLM calls use prompt caching. Measures spend structure directly and finds the management discipline the thesis describes largely absent in deployed systems.

Microsoft cut per-employee monthly AI caps from $100,000 to ~$10,000 and forecast Anthropic spend down by more than a third; Meta Claude Code users 60,000 to 30,000. Original reporting from internal figures (The Information)
Uber: per-engineer monthly spend tiers needing manager approval to exceed, internal gateway tracking spend and audit per user; company's own account, not independently checked
Orosz interviews at 27 workplaces: AI spend per developer from a $150 monthly cap to ~$3,000; caps and spend-versus-PR-throughput discussed per company
OpenAI telemetry: median researcher >$600/day of inference, p90 >$7,000, 3.1 agent-workdays per human workday; a frontier lab where agent spend is salary-scale

Jellyfish survey of 635+ leaders: 42% name rising AI tool expense as the top adoption challenge, ahead of security, quality, training. Measures concern about spend, not how spend is planned or attributed, so no direction

reachRationale: The change has moved from maximising token use to cost consciousness across independent contexts: caps and approval tiers at Uber, Microsoft and Meta; a 27-company survey showing caps from $150 to about $3,000 a month per developer; and an institution, the Tokenomics Foundation, backed by ten large enterprises. Per-task cost analyses show the unit of account being renegotiated in public. Counter-evidence (most agentic requests are simple) concerns how spend is distributed, not whether organisations now manage it.
whatWouldChangeThis: Per-developer spend flattens for two consecutive quarters despite continued adoption, making the line item unremarkable
Vendors move decisively to flat per-seat pricing, removing the variable component that forces the management question

developmentPaths.title: Managed machine expenditure
developmentPaths.description: Spend is attributed, budgeted and reviewed like any other operating cost, with named owners.

developmentPaths.title: Compute abundance
developmentPaths.description: Prices fall far enough that the spend stops being worth managing and the question disappears.

developmentPaths.title: Two-tier access
developmentPaths.description: Well-funded organisations run machine work freely while others ration it, widening capability gaps.

construct: Whether engineering organisations plan, attribute, cap and justify the cost of machine work as a managed operating expense, and how that spend relates to what it delivers per task. Not model price cuts, total AI adoption, or benchmark scores, all of which move without any organisation changing how it accounts for or approves machine spend.
